skill.name: compress
skill.description: Compress natural language memory files into a shorter caveman style while preserving code blocks, URLs, paths, headings, and backups.
skill.summary: Compress markdown or text memory files to reduce token usage while preserving technical content.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, validation regexes, and denylist comments for sensitive files. Confirmed risks remain because the skill reads an Anthropic API key, sends selected file contents to Claude, can fall back to the Claude CLI, and overwrites the target file with model output after backup.

remediation.issue: Natural language file contents are sent to an external LLM service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each compression and warn that file contents leave the local machine.

remediation.issue: Model output overwrites the original file after only structural validation.
remediation.suggestion: Write compressed output to a separate file first or require confirmation before replacing the original.

remediation.issue: Sensitive-file blocking relies on filename and path heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Add content scanning for common credential formats before sending text to Claude, and keep refusing on uncertain matches.

remediation.issue: The Claude CLI fallback executes an external command.
remediation.suggestion: Document the fallback clearly and keep the subprocess invocation shell-free with fixed arguments.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Content Sent to External LLM and Written Back
semantic_findings.description: compress.py embeds the original file text in a prompt sent to Claude, then writes the model output over the original path after creating a backup. Sensitive-path denylist checks reduce exposure, but ordinary prose files may still contain private information and prompt-injection text that can alter the compressed result.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly places original file content into an LLM prompt and writes the returned text to disk. The backup and validation reduce data-loss risk, but they do not remove the third-party disclosure or prompt-injection risk.

content.value_statement: Long memory files consume context and make repeated AI sessions expensive. This skill compresses markdown and text memory files while preserving technical details, code, URLs, and structure.
actual_capabilities: Compresses markdown and text files into shorter caveman-style prose.
Preserves fenced code blocks, inline code, URLs, file paths, commands, and headings.
Detects code and configuration files and skips them instead of modifying them.
Creates a human-readable backup before replacing the original file.
Validates headings, code blocks, URLs, paths, and bullet counts after compression.
Retries targeted fixes when validation finds structural errors.
limitations: Sends eligible file contents to Claude through the API or CLI.
Only supports natural language files such as markdown and text.
Filename-based sensitive-file detection can miss secrets inside ordinary prose files.
Compressed prose may be less readable for humans than the original.

use_cases.title: Reduce project memory size
use_cases.description: Compress a long CLAUDE.md file so agents spend fewer tokens reading repeated project instructions.

use_cases.title: Shorten planning notes
use_cases.description: Turn verbose markdown notes into compact action-oriented text while keeping paths, commands, and examples intact.

use_cases.title: Maintain compact team preferences
use_cases.description: Compress preference and todo files that are loaded often across AI coding sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Compress one memory file
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this memory file: <absolute filepath>. Preserve code, links, commands, and headings exactly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use with a single markdown memory file.

prompt_templates.title: Compress a project instruction file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use caveman compression on my CLAUDE.md file. Stop if the file is not natural language or if a backup already exists.

prompt_templates.title: Compress notes while preserving structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this markdown notes file into caveman style. Keep headings, bullets, code blocks, URLs, paths, and commands unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed notes with mixed technical content.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a compression result
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this file and verify the result. If validation fails, restore the original and report the validation errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow where data preservation matters.

output_examples.input: A verbose project instruction file with repeated guidance and examples.
output_examples.output: A shorter markdown file that keeps the same headings, examples, commands, and links, plus a backup of the original.

output_examples.input: A code or configuration file path is provided by mistake.
output_examples.output: The skill reports that the file is not natural language and skips compression without modifying it.

output_examples.input: A markdown file contains code blocks and URLs.
output_examples.output: The prose is shortened while code blocks and URLs remain unchanged.

best_practices: Review the file for private information before compression because contents may be sent to Claude.
Keep the generated backup until you confirm the compressed file is accurate.
Use the skill on markdown or text memory files, not source code or configuration files.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill on secrets, credentials, private keys, or personal data.
Do not compress files when exact human-readable wording is required.
Do not delete the backup before checking that important details were preserved.

faq.question: What files can this skill compress?
faq.answer: It is designed for markdown and text files that contain natural language, such as CLAUDE.md, todos, and preference files.

faq.question: Does it modify code blocks?
faq.answer: No. The prompt and validation are designed to preserve fenced code blocks and inline code exactly.

faq.question: Does it create a backup?
faq.answer: Yes. It saves the original file as a .original.md backup before writing the compressed version.

faq.question: Does it send file contents to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends eligible file contents to Claude through the Anthropic API or the Claude CLI.

faq.question: Can it compress configuration files?
faq.answer: No. It skips common code and configuration extensions, including JSON, YAML, TOML, shell scripts, and .env files.

faq.question: What happens if validation fails?
faq.answer: The skill retries targeted fixes. If retries fail, it restores the original file and removes the backup.
